newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico farm support seen at 25 bln pesos in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico farm support seen at 25 bln pesos in 1997.

text.p: Mexico is seen increasing its farm support bill to 25 billion pesos in 1997 from the 18 billion pesos expected to be thrown at agriculture this year, a top private-sector farm leader said Monday.

Miguel Castro, chairman of the National Farming Council, told reporters he expected the government to increase the bill for farm subsidies because it needed to keep the cash incentives to work land in line with inflation.

"On top of that, we aspire that the government will increase the amount of support next year," Castro said, adding President Ernesto Zedillo had singled out the countryside as one economic area where Mexico could forge ahead.

Mexico's main agriculture support system in called Procampo and basically subsidizes farmers directly with cash payments to encourage plantings and increased productivity. It is focusses on 11 basic crops, including grains.
